rounds.text: Trescon Ltd is demonstrating explosive top-line and bottom-line acceleration, with compounded sales growth reaching 298% and compounded profit growth hitting 145% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. This phenomenal expansion is translating into tangible operational improvement, highlighted by a dramatic quarterly operating margin surge to 15% in June 2026, marking a massive 15 percentage point expansion over the year-ago quarter [E22]. Furthermore, profit growth is actively outpacing 1-year price growth by 183%, demonstrating that the company is beginning to outperform stale market expectations as results score a stellar 100 out of 100 [E40, E54]. Patient investors can acquire this high-growth story at a deep asset discount, with the stock trading at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.39x against a book value of ₹ 18.9, while management alignment is simultaneously strengthening through insider accumulation as promoters increased their stake to 48.15% [E2, E32]. Finally, the business maintains a comfortable short-term liquidity buffer with a current ratio of 3.91x, giving it ample operational runway to execute its turnaround [E29]. conceded: [E1], [E36], [E53].

Despite reported sales and profit growth, Trescon Ltd exhibits severe fundamental weaknesses and an overextended valuation that the underlying returns fail to justify [E14, E15, E53]. The company suffers from deeply depressed profitability, posting a return on equity of -0.55% against a sector benchmark of 4.26%, and a three-year median return on equity of -1% [E9, E19]. Furthermore, cash generation has detached entirely from reported earnings, evidenced by a negative operating cash flow of Rs -4.26 Cr and a negative free cash flow of Rs -6.22 Cr for Mar 2026 [E26, E27]. Financial risk is compounding as borrowings have more than doubled to Rs 47.26 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 20.10 Cr a year prior, accompanied by warning flags that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E30, E44]. Valuation is stretched by a high P/E ratio of 76x compared to a sector benchmark of 22.54x, and a discounted cash flow model suggests the stock is significantly overvalued with a margin of safety of -191.7% [E1, E6, E37]. Conceded: compounded sales growth stands at 298% and compounded profit growth at 145% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15].

The bear relies on historical returns and cash flow snapshots that overlook the explosive operating inflection underway [E14, E15, E22]. Conceded: operating cash flow was Rs -4.26 Cr in Mar 2026 and borrowings increased to Rs 47.26 Cr [E26, E30]. However, this capital expansion is fueling staggering top-line growth of 298% and profit growth of 145% in the trailing twelve months, demonstrating that demand is scaling rapidly [E14, E15]. Quarterly data reveals that this growth is accelerating aggressively, with operating margin surging to 15% in June 2026 from just 1% in the year-ago quarter [E22]. Furthermore, the market is pricing the stock at a steep discount of just 0.39x book value, ignoring the fact that profit growth is currently outpacing 1-year price growth by 183% [E2, E40]. Promoters have recognized this deep mispricing, increasing their stake to 48.15% by September 2026 [E32]. Finally, short-term liquidity remains exceptionally comfortable with a current ratio of 3.91x, providing ample cushion to execute the ongoing turnaround [E29].

Conceded: the trailing twelve months show robust top-line and profit growth of 298% and 145% [E14, E15], and quarterly operating margin rose to 15% in June 2026 [E22]. However, the bull's reliance on capital expansion masking negative cash flows fails when examined against actual operational output: operating cash flow hit negative Rs -4.26 Cr and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs -6.22 Cr in March 2026 [E26, E27]. This severe cash burn directly coincides with borrowings climbing sharply to Rs 47.26 Cr from Rs 20.10 Cr a year earlier [E30]. Furthermore, the bull's citation of a 0.39x price-to-book ratio [E2] ignores the underlying poor quality of earnings, which are bloated by Rs 1.98 Cr of other income [E45] and potential interest cost capitalization [E44]. Finally, the reverse DCF demonstrates that the current price already aggressively prices in 25.2% earnings growth against a base-case assumption of just 10.0% [E38], leaving no margin of safety at -191.7% [E37].
